meta.title: RSU Taxes: Delivery Withholding Versus Sale Basis
meta.heading: RSU Taxes: Delivery Withholding Versus Sale Basis
meta.description: RSU withholding and final tax are different.
meta.cardIntro: RSU withholding and final tax are different. In a 2026 illustration, 100 delivered shares at $50 create $5,000 wage income. With $1,100 federal withholding and $400 other allocated withholding, retained value is $3,500, or 70 shares at that same price.

rsu-tax.intro: Use delivery mode for a simple stock-settled award with simultaneous vesting and delivery, or use sale mode for an already-taxed known lot. The two calculations answer different questions and keep payroll wage value, withholding, adjusted basis and capital gain separate.
rsu-tax.answer: RSU withholding and final tax are different. In a 2026 illustration, 100 delivered shares at $50 create $5,000 wage income. With $1,100 federal withholding and $400 other allocated withholding, retained value is $3,500, or 70 shares at that same price.
rsu-tax.exampleNote: Original 2026 illustrations checked against independent high-precision arithmetic and stated source mechanics. IRS example prices are identified where used; dates are illustrative. No complete tax return, actual payroll result or professional review is claimed.

sections.title: Which value becomes wage income?
paragraphs: The supported case uses the FMV of nonrestricted shares when delivered, with vesting and settlement occurring together. The example’s 100 shares at 50 create 5,000 in wage income before withholding. A grant-date quote is not the basis for this calculation.
Private-company double-trigger awards, delayed settlement, special payroll timing and qualified deferral elections need plan-specific analysis. They are outside the worksheet.
sections.formula: Delivery wages = gross shares × income-date FMV. Sale basis = shares sold × FMV already included as wages. Capital gain = net sale proceeds − allocated basis.

sections.title: Why can 22% be less than final tax?
paragraphs: The optional 2026 federal supplemental-wage method is a withholding method, not the taxpayer’s final rate. It applies only under the stated payroll conditions. The part of annual supplemental wages above 1 million is subject to 37% withholding.

With 998,000 already paid, the current 5,000 award splits into 2,000 at 22% and 3,000 at 37%, giving 1,550 federal withholding. The actual-withholding option lets you use a known payroll figure when the optional method does not fit.

sections.title: What does the other-withholding input include?
paragraphs: Enter the dollar amount actually allocated or separately estimated for employee payroll, state or local withholding. The calculator does not determine those taxes, wage bases or state rules.

These amounts reduce retained value but are not subtracted when comparing assumed federal income tax with federal income-tax withholding. A federal difference is not a promised refund or an estimated-payment instruction.

sections.title: How is a later sale different from delivery income?
paragraphs: A later sale compares net proceeds with the income-date basis of the shares sold. For 70 shares with 50 basis each, selling at 80 with 10 fees gives 2,090 capital gain. The original wage value is not charged a second time.
Use a known lot and its actual nonrestricted acquisition date. Withholding does not reduce basis per share. A broker’s reported basis and plan supplemental records should be reconciled before filing.

sections.title: What remains an assumption?
paragraphs: Net shares are only an equivalent at the income-date price. Actual share withholding, sell-to-cover execution, fractional-share rules and cash funding can differ.

Sale mode uses your entered short/long rate only on positive gain. It does not net losses, compute a full federal return, add NIIT, choose a tax lot or price a future sale. The separate capital-gains tool can model a broader tax scenario once the basis and baseline income are known.

questions.question: Is the grant date the capital holding-period start?
questions.answer: Not for the supported RSU share-delivery case. Use the date nonrestricted shares were actually acquired; deferred arrangements require separate review.

questions.question: Does withholding reduce the basis per share?
questions.answer: No. Under these assumptions the income-date FMV included in wages supplies basis. The number of shares left after withholding and the basis of each share are different matters.

questions.question: Does a negative federal difference guarantee a refund?
questions.answer: No. It only compares one rate-based assumption with federal withholding allocated to the award. The complete return can differ.

meta.title: ESPP Taxes: Disposition Dates, Compensation and Adjusted Basis
meta.heading: ESPP Taxes: Disposition Dates, Compensation and Adjusted Basis
meta.description: A Section 423 ESPP sale can contain both compensation and capital gain.
meta.cardIntro: A Section 423 ESPP sale can contain both compensation and capital gain. In the stated qualifying-date example, 100 shares bought for $68 have $1,500 compensation and $8,300 adjusted basis; selling at $120 with $10 fees leaves $3,690 capital gain.

espp-tax.intro: Choose known purchase data or one of two standard discount formulas, then inspect the date test and the separate capital holding term. The grant-date hypothetical exercise price matters for qualifying treatment; it is not always the actual lookback purchase price.
espp-tax.answer: A Section 423 ESPP sale can contain both compensation and capital gain. In the stated qualifying-date example, 100 shares bought for $68 have $1,500 compensation and $8,300 adjusted basis; selling at $120 with $10 fees leaves $3,690 capital gain.
espp-tax.exampleNote: Original 2026 illustrations checked against independent high-precision arithmetic and stated source mechanics. IRS example prices are identified where used; dates are illustrative. No complete tax return, actual payroll result or professional review is claimed.

sections.title: Which prices do I need from the plan records?
paragraphs: Use grant-date FMV, exercise-date FMV, actual price paid and the grant-date option price determined as if exercised then. Form 3922 box 8 supplies the hypothetical price when applicable; if the price was fixed and that box is blank, use the fixed option price.

For a 15% lower-FMV lookback with grant FMV 100 and purchase FMV 80, actual price is 68 and the grant-date as-if price is 85. Replacing both with 68 would distort the qualifying compensation calculation.
sections.formula: Adjusted basis = purchase cost + compensation included in income. Capital result = net sale proceeds − adjusted basis. Compensation + capital result = economic gain/loss before tax.

sections.title: Why are there two different holding-period questions?
paragraphs: The Section 423 date test uses both the two-year grant period and one-year exercise/transfer period. This date-only worksheet requires sale after both anniversaries and flags exact-anniversary reliance for record review. Exercise and share transfer are assumed to be the same entered date.

Capital term is separate and uses the holding period after acquisition. A sale can fail the two-year grant condition while already producing long-term capital gain. Employment and plan qualification are assumed from confirmed records, not established by dates alone.

sections.title: How does compensation differ between qualifying and disqualifying sales?
paragraphs: For qualifying dates, compensation is limited to the smaller of the grant-date hypothetical discount and the sale-date FMV gain over actual price, with a floor of zero. Gross sale price is assumed to equal sale-date FMV; commissions affect the capital result.

For disqualifying dates, compensation is the positive purchase-date FMV spread. It is not capped at sale gain. That differs from the ISO rule and can leave compensation income alongside a capital loss.

sections.title: How does adjusted basis prevent double counting?
paragraphs: Add compensation included in income once to original purchase cost, then subtract the adjusted basis from net proceeds. In the main example: 6,800 cost + 1,500 compensation = 8,300 basis; 11,990 net proceeds − 8,300 = 3,690 capital gain.

The reconciliation is compensation plus capital result equals economic gain before tax. Check W-2, Form 3922 and supplemental broker records before using a reported 1099-B basis. The worksheet does not prepare Form 8949 or a tax return.

sections.title: Is the tax estimate a complete recommendation?
paragraphs: No. The optional rates are your incremental assumptions. The model taxes compensation and positive capital gain separately, preserves losses and does not automatically offset them against other income or infer carryforwards.

It does not test the Section 423 25,000 grant-date accrual limit, model every plan formula, add state taxes or payroll tax, determine nonresident treatment or advise a hold/sell decision. Section 423 compensation is not passed through the RSU supplemental-wage withholding method.

questions.question: Is every ESPP a Section 423 plan?
questions.answer: No. Nonqualified and non-U.S. plans can differ. This tool stops for nonqualified or unconfirmed plan treatment.

questions.question: Can a disqualifying sale still have long-term capital gain?
questions.answer: Yes. The grant two-year test can fail while the share purchase holding period exceeds one year. Compensation and capital term remain separate.

questions.question: Does the capital loss automatically cancel compensation tax?
questions.answer: No automatic offset is modeled. Netting, deduction limits and carryforwards depend on the complete return.

questions.question: Do I use the actual purchase price as the grant-date option price?
questions.answer: Only if the plan records establish that it was fixed at that same price. Lookback plans often require a distinct grant-date hypothetical price.
